why: A = IsGenCompactHomotopy.isCompact_solutionSet_restrict (universes 0): the restricted problems have compact solution sets. This is a corollary of the definition and says nothing about whether the definition is correct. B says the project's IsGenCompactHomotopy equals B's notion. The two definitions differ in one clause only. B asks for a tame strong bundle: IsTameStrongBundle = PX.IsTame plus an EQUIVALENT strong bundle atlas whose base retractions are all tame. The project asks only PX.IsTame (tame retracts), plus tame germ data at smooth points for f and each f|X_τ (IsScFredholmSectionTame, the germ reading, the same notion B uses). All other clauses agree literally (solSet = solutionSet; the instance, inclusion and IsSection arguments are propositions). Proved: B-notion ⇒ project notion (project_of_B); project notion + IsTameStrongBundle ⇒ B-notion (B_of_project); hence B ↔ 'every bundle carrying a project homotopy is a tame strong bundle' (B_iff_tame). That last statement is believed true: over a tame chart, a strong bundle chart can be rebuilt as R'(u,h) = (r'(u), Γ(σ r'(u), h)) with r' tame. But the project has no such construction, and building it (new charts, compatibility, atlas equivalence) is substantial glue. B ⇒ A is vacuous: A is re-proved directly in a few lines.
